_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a real drill sentence from that point. 'nonstandard': entries hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle — forms that break or sit outside the regular patterns.

entries.label: Present
entries.usage: What someone does now or does regularly. The ending changes with who is doing it.
entries.example: Я читаю книгу. — I am reading a book.

entries.label: Past
entries.usage: What already happened. The ending follows the doer's gender and number, not the person.
entries.example: Она была в Москве. — She was in Moscow.

entries.label: Future (ongoing)
entries.usage: What will be happening — быть + the action, for processes without a finish line.
entries.example: Завтра я буду работать дома. — Tomorrow I will be working at home.

entries.label: Future (completed)
entries.usage: What will get done — one word, present-style endings on the perfective verb.
entries.example: Я позвоню тебе вечером. — I will call you in the evening.

entries.label: Aspect choice
entries.usage: The process verb or the result verb — читать vs прочитать. The heart of the Russian verb.
entries.example: Вчера я наконец прочитал эту книгу. — Yesterday I finally finished reading this book.

entries.label: Commands
entries.usage: Telling someone to do something — informal читай, polite or plural читайте.
entries.example: Скажите, пожалуйста, где метро? — Please tell me, where is the metro?

entries.label: Reflexives (-ся)
entries.usage: Verbs that fold back on their subject — the -ся tail stays through every form.
entries.example: Я занимаюсь русским языком. — I study the Russian language.

entries.label: Would (бы)
entries.usage: Wishes and what-ifs — past form + бы makes 'would'.
entries.example: Я хотел бы чашку кофе. — I would like a cup of coffee.

entries.point: Verbs of motion: идти vs ходить
entries.label: Going on foot
entries.usage: Two different verbs for walking: one trip in progress (идти) vs trips in general (ходить).
entries.example: Сейчас я иду в школу. — I am walking to school right now.

entries.point: Verbs of motion: ехать vs ездить
entries.label: Going by vehicle
entries.usage: Riding or driving splits the same way: one trip (ехать) vs habitual travel (ездить).
entries.example: Сейчас мы едем в Москву. — We are on our way to Moscow now.

entries.point: Prefixed verbs of motion (прийти, уйти, выйти)
entries.label: Arriving & leaving
entries.usage: Prefixes aim the motion — при- arrives, у- departs, вы- exits — and flip the aspect.
entries.example: Он пришёл домой в семь часов. — He came home at seven o'clock.

entries.label: In order to
entries.usage: Why you are doing something, when one person does both halves — чтобы plus the plain dictionary verb.
entries.example: Я учу русский, чтобы работать в Москве. — I am learning Russian in order to work in Moscow.

entries.label: Wishes (чтобы)
entries.usage: Wanting somebody ELSE to do something — чтобы, then the verb in its past form however future the wish is.
entries.example: Я хочу, чтобы ты пришёл завтра. — I want you to come tomorrow (said to a man).

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: Passing on what was said — что for statements, ли for a yes/no question, and the original words keep their own time.
entries.example: Он сказал, что придёт завтра. — He said that he would come tomorrow.

entries.label: Must / may
entries.usage: Sentences with nobody doing the doing — надо, можно, нельзя, and whoever it applies to goes into the 'to me' form.
entries.example: Мне надо идти домой. — I have to go home.

entries.point: Aspect in the imperative and prohibitions
entries.label: Aspect in commands
entries.usage: Which command verb to reach for — the finished one asks for a single act, the ongoing one invites, encourages, and says 'don't'.
entries.example: Не опаздывай — урок начинается в девять. — Don't be late — the lesson starts at nine.

entries.label: Have you ever…
entries.usage: When only the bare fact matters — ever read it, already seen it — the ongoing verb covers even finished events.
entries.example: Вы читали «Войну и мир»? — Да, давно. — Have you read War and Peace? — Yes, long ago.

entries.point: Aspect nuance: annulled results (открывал vs открыл)
entries.label: Undone actions
entries.usage: The choice that says whether the result still stands — открывал means it was opened and shut again, открыл means it is still open.
entries.example: Здесь холодно — кто-то открывал окно, но уже закрыл. — It's cold in here — someone had the window open, but has already closed it.

entries.label: Verb prefixes
entries.usage: The front piece that redirects a verb — пере- does it again, до- takes it to the end, за- drops in for a moment.
entries.example: Книга так понравилась, что я хочу её перечитать. — I liked the book so much that I want to reread it.

entries.label: Is being done (строится)
entries.usage: Things that get done without naming who does them — the -ся tail carries 'is being built', 'is sold', 'is discussed'.
entries.example: Новая школа строится уже два года. — The new school has been under construction for two years.

entries.label: While doing (читая)
entries.usage: 'While doing' in one word, hooked onto a sentence whose subject is doing both things at once.
entries.example: Читая книгу, я делаю заметки. — While reading a book, I take notes.

entries.label: Having done (прочитав)
entries.usage: 'Having done' in one word — the first action finishes, and then the main one happens.
entries.example: Прочитав книгу, я вернул её в библиотеку. — Having read the book, I returned it to the library.

entries.label: Particles (же, ведь)
entries.usage: The small words that carry tone — же for 'I told you', ведь for 'you know this', -то for 'as for that'.
entries.example: Я же тебе говорил, что магазин закрыт! — I told you the shop was closed!

entries.label: Emphasis (именно)
entries.usage: Pointing hard at one word — именно он means HE was the one and nobody else.
entries.example: Именно он помог мне, когда все отказались. — It was he who helped me when everyone else refused.

entries.label: Prepositional (where)
entries.usage: Where something is — after в and на for locations, the noun's ending changes.
entries.example: Книга на столе. — The book is on the table.

entries.label: Accusative (what)
entries.usage: The thing the action lands on — feminine -а becomes -у, masculine things stay put.
entries.example: Я читаю книгу. — I am reading a book.

entries.label: Accusative (whom)
entries.usage: When the object is alive, masculine nouns borrow the genitive ending instead.
entries.example: Я вижу брата каждый день. — I see my brother every day.

entries.label: Genitive (whose)
entries.usage: Ownership and 'of' — the possessor follows the thing possessed, in genitive.
entries.example: Это машина брата. — This is my brother's car.

entries.label: Genitive (there's no…)
entries.usage: What's missing — нет always pulls the missing thing into the genitive.
entries.example: У меня нет времени. — I have no time.

entries.label: Dative (to whom)
entries.usage: The receiver — whoever something is given, said, or shown to takes the dative.
entries.example: Я даю брату книгу. — I am giving my brother a book.

entries.label: Instrumental (with what)
entries.usage: The tool or companion — writing with a pen, tea with sugar, going with a friend.
entries.example: Я пишу ручкой. — I write with a pen.

entries.label: Counting forms
entries.usage: Numbers boss the noun around: 2–4 take one form, 5+ another — час, часа, часов.
entries.example: Мне двадцать два года. — I am twenty-two years old.

entries.label: Gender
entries.usage: Every noun is a he, a she or an it — usually visible in its last letter, and the word that replaces it must match.
entries.example: Где книга? — Она на столе. — Where is the book? — It is on the table.

entries.label: This is (это)
entries.usage: Point at something and name it — Russian needs no word for 'is': Это дом, Это мой друг.
entries.example: Это мой друг. — This is my friend.

entries.point: Мне нравится — liking with the dative
entries.label: Liking (нравится)
entries.usage: Saying you like something turns the sentence round — you go into the 'to me' form and the thing you like drives the verb.
entries.example: Мне нравится этот фильм. — I like this film.

entries.label: Days and times
entries.usage: Saying when — в понедельник for days, в январе for months, and утром or зимой with no little word at all.
entries.example: У нас урок в понедельник. — We have a lesson on Monday.

entries.label: Dates
entries.usage: Giving the date — первое января for 'today is the first', второго марта for 'on the second'.
entries.example: Сегодня пятое мая. — Today is the fifth of May.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: Asking who, what, where, when, why and how — the question word goes first and the rest of the sentence stays as it was.
entries.example: Кто это? — Who is this?

entries.label: And / but
entries.usage: Joining two things — и adds more of the same, но objects, and а switches to something different.
entries.example: Я пью чай и кофе. — I drink tea and coffee.

entries.label: Nobody / nothing
entries.usage: Nobody, nothing, never — and the verb still keeps its не, because Russian wants the negative twice.
entries.example: Никто не пришёл на собрание. — Nobody came to the meeting.

entries.label: Numbers in other cases (пятидесяти)
entries.usage: Big numbers change their own endings too, once they follow words like 'about', 'with' or 'more than'.
entries.example: В зале было около пятидесяти человек. — There were about fifty people in the hall.

entries.label: Agreement
entries.usage: The adjective mirrors its noun — новый дом, новая книга, новое слово.
entries.example: Это новый дом. — This is a new house.

entries.label: Comparatives
entries.usage: More and -er — usually -ее on the stem, with a few classics like лучше and больше.
entries.example: Эта книга интереснее, чем фильм. — This book is more interesting than the film.

entries.label: Superlatives
entries.usage: The most — самый in front, agreeing with the noun like any adjective.
entries.example: Москва — самый большой город России. — Moscow is the biggest city in Russia.

entries.label: Short forms
entries.usage: A clipped predicate form — рад, рада, рады — only after 'to be', never before a noun.
entries.example: Я очень рад тебя видеть. — I am very glad to see you.

entries.label: My / your / our
entries.usage: Possessives agree like adjectives — мой дом, моя книга, моё окно.
entries.example: Это моя книга. — This is my book.

entries.label: Свой (one's own)
entries.usage: The boomerang possessive — points back at the subject, whoever that is.
entries.example: Я люблю свою работу. — I love my (own) job.

entries.label: Который (which)
entries.usage: The word for who, which or that — it borrows gender from the thing described and its ending from the job it does in the second half.
entries.example: Вот книга, которую я читаю. — Here is the book that I am reading.

entries.label: Себя / сам
entries.usage: Pointing back at whoever the sentence is about — себя for himself as an object, сам for doing it personally.
entries.example: Он думает только о себе. — He thinks only about himself.

entries.label: Participle (who is doing)
entries.usage: A one-word way to say 'who is doing' — built off the они form and then worn like an adjective.
entries.example: Человек, читающий газету, — мой сосед. — The man reading the newspaper is my neighbour.

entries.label: Participle (who did)
entries.usage: A one-word 'who did' or 'who lived' — the past tense minus its -л, agreeing with its noun like an adjective.
entries.example: Писатель, живший в Париже, вернулся в Россию. — The writer who had lived in Paris returned to Russia.

entries.label: Participle (done to it)
entries.usage: A one-word 'that was done to it' — written, built, closed — describing the thing it happened to.
entries.example: Письмо, написанное вчера, уже пришло. — The letter written yesterday has already arrived.

entries.label: It is closed (закрыт)
entries.usage: The everyday way to say something has been done — закрыт, написано, сделана — standing after 'is', never in front of a noun.
entries.example: Магазин закрыт — приходите завтра. — The shop is closed — come back tomorrow.

entries.label: Instead of который
entries.usage: How written Russian squeezes a который clause down to a single describing word.
entries.example: Вопросы, обсуждаемые на собрании, были важными. — The questions being discussed at the meeting were important.

entries.label: Formal style
entries.usage: For reading contracts, notices and the news, where actions arrive as nouns instead of verbs — принятие решения, при рассмотрении вопроса.
entries.example: В сложившейся ситуации надо действовать быстро. — In the situation that has developed, one must act quickly.
